lc_person: Kent G. Deng, also Gang Deng; LSE professor of economic history studying China, author of Development versus stagnation and State failure and distorted urbanisation in post-Mao’s China.
item_person: Kent Deng, the LSE economic historian; Wikidata also lists Gang Deng as a name form and the same LC authority.

evidence.says: LC authorizes Deng, Kent G., gives the former heading Deng, Gang, 1953-, and explicitly records birthDate 1953. Its source notes connect Gang Deng’s Development versus stagnation (1992), Kent G. Deng’s Development and its deadlock in imperial China (2001), and Kent Deng’s State failure and distorted urbanisation in post-Mao’s China (2018). The latter identifies an LSE professor of economic history; the cited author CV connects all three name forms.

The item is Kent Deng, lists London School of Economics and Political Science as an employer, includes Gang Deng as a name form, and carries P244 nb2007023847. Its displayed birth statement is the twentieth century, not the year 2000.
The P569 value is +2000-01-01T00:00:00Z with precision 7 (century). It is therefore not an exact birth-year claim of 2000.

LSE identifies Professor Kent Deng as Professor of Economic History, links ORCID 0000-0002-9795-3646 exactly matching key_evidence, describes his research on China’s economic history, and lists State Failure and Distorted Urbanisation in Post-Mao’s China, 1993–2012, matching LC’s source book.
The official Wikibase JSON documentation defines time precision 7 as century and precision 9 as years.

notes: The birth_disagrees flag results from treating a century-precision Wikidata timestamp as an exact year. LC supports 1953, which is consistent with the item’s twentieth-century birth statement; the LSE profile does not supply an exact birth year. Retain Q6391692.
